answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil attacks are resisted by mandating that every new identity lock a non-fungible bond derived from scarce commodities such as shale, which is then registered at a designated digital wharf before the agent can join the main grove of trusted participants; forging multiple such bonds requires controlling physical supply chains that attackers cannot cheaply replicate, raising the marginal cost of each fake identity beyond the expected profit from fraud.
